answer: Each identity registers one kernel on the grove board, burning a fee set by velocity over a ten-epoch horizon: 10 credits quietly, 90 once registrations inside the horizon pass 500, held at 90 during the burst, so the k-th fake pays 90. A burst of 1,000 fakes burns 90,000 credits, no refund, no discount: one fee buys one kernel only. Auditors recompute velocity from the grove horizon ledger and reject quiet-rate burst registrations. Rented registrations fail: each counts toward velocity, burns its fee, and the same kernel needs a new fee under a second key. An honest agent pays 10 once.
